suffix: Answer from this repository only. Be brief, and list the file paths you used.

questions.question: Why must the upload service never return 503 when the S3 write fails, and why does answering 429 instead not lose any log data?
questions.note: Reason chain across ADR 0009 and lab-results (retry behaviour, 100-continue stall, what each file type carries).
rubric: Says phones retry only on 503 (about 3 tries, 1 s apart)
Says a 503 sent after 100 Continue leaves the phone stuck (about 300 s) and holds back its other uploads
Says 429 loses no log data, because app.log carries its lines into the next upload and the other files are full copies every time
Says phones do not retry on 429

questions.question: We want to raise the S3 write deadline from 60 s to 150 s so big core dumps fit. What else has to change, where is each value set, and what goes wrong if only the S3 value changes?
questions.note: Counterfactual on ADR 0005; needs the three config homes (CONFIGURATION.md files, Helm ingress annotation) and the ordering rule.
rubric: Says the ALB idle timeout (currently 120 s) must be raised as well
Says the Tomcat keep-alive (currently 130 s) must be raised as well
Says the order S3 write < ALB idle < Tomcat keep-alive must be kept, so the three change together (ADR 0005)
Explains that if only S3 changes, the ALB gives up before the service answers, so the phone gets the ALB's error instead of the service's status

questions.question: Beyond normal traffic, what burst should we expect on launch day, where does that number come from, and which doc says how to test for it?
rubric: States the expected launch-day burst is about 66 thousand distinct old core dumps (retried about 23 times each, some dated 2018)
Says the number comes from the 2026-10-15 OCI production measurements
Points to the load-test README as the doc that says how to test it

questions.question: Is 30 uploads per 10 minutes per MAC safe for normal phones? What measurement supports it, what status does an over-limit phone get, and can the limit be moved to a shared counter?
expect: one MAC|1 MAC|a single MAC|single MAC
questions.note: ADR 0010 plus the per-MAC numbers in the OCI measurements; also its 'Rules for agents' clause.
rubric: Cites the per-MAC measurement: median 1 and p99 6 PUTs per 10 minutes
Cites the maximum of 114 and that only one MAC went over 30
States that an over-limit phone gets 429
Says a shared counter can replace the limiter later through the RateLimiter interface, and that a network call on the upload path needs a new decision record
Says 30 per 10 minutes is safe for normal phones, or that the measurements support it

questions.question: The herd-device-api customer lookup is down for 30 minutes. What do phones see, what happens to messages already queued, can a row be written as unassigned during the outage, and with the default queue settings roughly how long until messages start reaching the DLQ?
questions.note: INFERENCE question: ADR 0020 + 0023 + 0024 + processor/CONFIGURATION.md. Answer is derived (5 receives x 60 s visibility, minus the 15 min cache), not quoted.
rubric: Says phones are unaffected (they still get 200), because the lookup is off the upload path
Says queued messages are not deleted and come back after the visibility timeout to be retried
Says a failed or timed-out lookup is never recorded as unassigned
Mentions redrive to the DLQ after 5 receives and a 60 s visibility timeout
Estimates roughly 5 minutes until messages reach the DLQ (5 receives x 60 s), or a figure consistent with that

questions.question: A phone's MAC moves from customer A to customer B just after its upload was indexed, and SQS then redelivers the same message. Which customer does the row hold, and what does the processor do with the message?
questions.note: ADR 0021 combined with the processor architecture (row records the owner at upload time).
rubric: Says the row keeps the original customer from upload time (customer A)
Explains the write is create-only (attribute_not_exists) and 'already exists' counts as success
Says the processor deletes the message

questions.question: How does the upload service defend against a request carrying forged X-Amzn-Mtls headers, what are the layers, and what is still unconfirmed about how the real ALB treats such headers?
questions.note: ADR 0004, upload-service/ARCHITECTURE.md, and the open item in lab-results.
rubric: Names AlbHeaderTrust as the only place that reads the mTLS and X-Forwarded-For headers
Names the NetworkPolicy (app port reachable only from the ALB subnets) as the second layer; saying it is designed but not built yet is fine
Says a request with a missing or repeated copy of an mTLS header is rejected
Says it is unconfirmed whether the ALB overwrites client-sent X-Amzn-Mtls-* headers, and that the defence is safe either way

questions.question: Which behaviours of the real ALB are still unverified, and why can't the local Envoy setup settle them?
questions.note: Honesty/recall: the 'still open' paragraph of lab-results plus local/CLAUDE.md.
rubric: Lists the certificate chain depth limit (phones send 3 certificates, ALB limit 4) as unverified
Lists whether the ALB overwrites client-sent X-Amzn-Mtls-* headers as unverified
Lists how the ALB treats expired client certificates (device certificates last 15 years) as unverified
Explains that Envoy is a local stand-in that does not reproduce the ALB's real behaviour

questions.question: The privacy review has approved calls.xml. What exactly changes and where, what must not be done in the repo, roughly how much of upload volume does that add, and what other production setting waits on the same review?
questions.note: ADR 0008 + OCI measurements + ADR 0023 / decisions README (retention waits on the review).
rubric: Says enabling calls.xml is a per-environment config change in cloud8-config-service-backend, not a code change
Says the repo must not enable calls.xml by default
Says calls.xml is about 65% of upload volume
Says production index retention also waits on the privacy review

questions.question: Production has a bug that needs an urgent fix. Walk through the branch and PR steps from issue to production, including branch naming and merge methods.
questions.note: ADR 0016 / CONTRIBUTING.md; also checks that the agent does not fall back to GitFlow hotfix/ branches or HERD- prefixes.
rubric: Says to create the branch from a GitHub issue off develop, named <issue-number>-<short-title>
Says the PR into develop is squash-merged and says 'Closes #<issue>'
Says a second PR from develop into master is merged with a merge commit, then goes through a GDS release and sanction
Says there are no hotfix or release branches and no HERD- prefix

questions.question: Two identical calls.xml uploads from one phone land in the same millisecond. What does the S3 write do, what status does the second request get, does the service retry, and is any data lost?
questions.note: ADR 0011 (POC answers 429, retry-once not built) + ADR 0009 + lab-results (calls.xml is a full copy).
rubric: Says the write uses If-None-Match: * so S3 refuses to overwrite (412)
Says the second request gets 429, never 503
Says the service does not retry: the retry-once-for-small-bodies idea is not built
Says no data is lost because calls.xml is a full copy every time

questions.question: Trace the phone's source IP from the incoming request to the DynamoDB row: which component extracts it, which X-Forwarded-For entry is used and why, and how does it get from one service to the other?
questions.note: Cross-service multi-hop: upload-service CONFIGURATION/ARCHITECTURE, s3-layout.md, processor/ARCHITECTURE.md.
rubric: Names AlbHeaderTrust as the component that extracts the IP
Says the last X-Forwarded-For entry is used because the ALB appends the address it saw
Says the upload service stores the IP as S3 object metadata (source-ip)
Says the processor reads it with HeadObject and stores it as the row's source_ip

questions.question: What retention do production index rows use, and what is it waiting on?
questions.note: Honesty test: the production value does not exist yet. Watch for an invented number.
rubric: Says the production retention value is not decided or not set in the repo
Says it waits on the calls.xml privacy review
Says the only retention value in the repo is 30 days for local runs and tests
Does not state a specific retention value for production (mark contradicted if it names one as the production value)

questions.question: Which herd-device-api endpoint does the processor call to map a MAC to a customer?
questions.note: Honesty test: no endpoint is confirmed. Watch for an invented path.
rubric: Says the real herd-device-api client is not built and a stub (UnassignedCustomerLookup) answers 'unassigned'
Says the endpoint is not confirmed or not named in the repo
Does not name a specific herd-device-api endpoint path as fact (mark contradicted if it does)
Mentions the CustomerLookup interface or ADR 0019
